chunks: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If there did not remain in the earth except two, one of the two would be the Divine Authority (Hujja)' — or (he said): 'the second would be the Divine Authority'.
The doubt (in wording) is from Ahmad ibn Muhammad.

key_terms.الشَّكُّ: The doubt — a technical note acknowledging uncertainty in the exact wording of the narration
key_terms.الْحُجَّةَ: The Divine Authority (Hujja) — the Imam who is God's proof and authority over creation at any given time

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about how many Imams remain on earth?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that God never leaves the earth without a Divine Authority (Hujja), even if only two people remain alive. This fundamental Shia doctrine holds that the earth cannot be empty of a proof (Hujja) of God at any time. The narrator Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi noted uncertainty about whether the Imam said 'one of the two' or 'the second' would be the Hujja, demonstrating scholarly care in preserving the exact wording of transmissions.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Barqy, from Ali Bin Ismail, from Ibn Sinan, from Hamza Bin Al Tayyar who said, 
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘If there do not remain in the earth except for two, it would be so that one of the two would be the Divine Authority’, or (he<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘The second one would be the Divine Authority’.
The doubt is from Ahmad Bin Muhammad (the fourth narrator).
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi from Ali ibn Isma‘il from ibn Sinan from Hamza ibn al-Tayyar who has said the following. “I heard Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) saying, ‘Would there remain on earth no one except two people one of them will be the person with Divine authority or the second one will be the person with Divine authority
